title: A good name (Avot 4:13)
hook: three crowns, Torah, priesthood and kingship, and the crown of a good name above them all
tomorrow: can you learn it just as well from home? Rabbi Nehorai says no.

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua's ladder: your student's honor as dear as your own. Honor the student. Today, one more crown, then the week comes back.

A diploma on a wall, a title in an email signature, a seat at the head of the table. All crowns, of a kind. Rabbi Shimon counts three big ones: the crown of Torah, the crown of priesthood, the crown of kingship. And then he names a fourth, and says it rises above all three. Which one can anyone wear? The one nobody hands you.
screen: `A TITLE. A DIPLOMA. A SEAT.` → `THREE CROWNS.` → `AND ONE ABOVE THEM.`

segments.voice: Here's Rabbi Shimon, in plain words. There are three crowns: Torah, priesthood and kingship. But the crown of a good name rises above them all. Priesthood came by birth. Kingship came by line or by power. Torah, learning, comes by long work. A good name comes from none of those. It's built by how you treat people when it costs you something, and it can't be inherited or bought. That's why it rises above the rest: the other crowns are worn on the head, and this one is worn in other people's mouths. Now the week, because a good name is made of it. Only one judges alone: ask a second pair of eyes. Poor or rich: the thin weeks build the habit. Less business: cut on purpose. Make an advocate: each good deed speaks for you. For heaven's sake endures: name what the gathering is for. And honor the student: guard the dignity of the newest person in the room. Six sayings. Put them together and you get a good name.
screen: `TORAH, PRIESTHOOD, KINGSHIP.` · `A GOOD NAME RISES ABOVE THEM.` · `WORN IN OTHER PEOPLE'S MOUTHS.` · `THE WEEK, IN SIX SAYINGS.` · then, large: `A GOOD NAME.`

segments.voice: Say your own full name out loud, once, slowly, as if someone were introducing you to a room. Then sit with what you'd want the room to hear right after it: one plain thing about how you treat people.
screen: `SAY YOUR FULL NAME.` · `WHAT COMES RIGHT AFTER IT?`

howItsDone: In Jewish tradition a person's good name, shem tov, is guarded closely, and the laws against gossip and shaming in public are part of protecting other people's names, too.

chat.meaning: Rabbi Shimon's fourth crown, a good name, rises above Torah, priesthood and kingship. It's made of deeds people remember.

Rabbi Shimon.meaning: the sage of the Mishnah who names the three crowns

Torah.meaning: God's teaching; here, learning as a crown

priesthood.meaning: the role of the kohanim, Aaron's descendants, in the Temple

kingship.meaning: the crown of a king, by line or by power
